title: Knowledge of simple intelligence: God's natural knowledge of all possibles, prior to every decree
source_text: IX. Per scientiam vero simplicis intelligentiae significant eam qua Deus novit & intelligit omnia possibilia rerumque essentias & connexiones omnes, seu necessarias, sive quomodocunque possibiles. Atque haec scientia dicitur naturalis, non libera; quia praecedit, juxta nostrum concipiendi modum, omne Dei decretum de rebus faciendis: neque potuit in Deo non esse, quanquam nihil extra se creare voluisset.
pass_a_gloss: IX. But by knowledge of simple intelligence they signify that by which God knows and understands all possibles and the essences of things and all connexions, whether necessary, or possible in any way whatever. And this knowledge is called natural, not free; because it precedes, according to our mode of conceiving, every decree of God concerning things to be made: nor could it not be in God, although he had willed to create nothing outside himself.
pass_b_english: By the knowledge of simple intelligence they mean the knowledge by which God knows and understands everything possible, the essences of things, and all their connections, whether necessary or possible in any way at all.

This knowledge is called natural rather than free. In our way of conceiving, it comes before every decree of God about the things to be made. It could not have been absent from God even if he had willed to create nothing outside himself.

lemmas.gloss: all possibles and the essences of things and all connexions

choices.why: The Schools' name for God's natural knowledge of all possibles; kept as a technical term.
